findings.title: Cleartext HTTP API base URL baked into every build profile
findings.description: expo.extra.apiBaseUrl = http://192.168.0.13:8080/api (also the fallback in src/api/config.js:8). eas.json has no per-profile override, so preview/production builds inherit a plaintext-HTTP LAN URL.
findings.exploit_scenario: Today: anyone on the same Wi-Fi as a dev/Expo Go tester runs a passive capture and reads the JWT, login credentials, chat messages and emergency-contact numbers in cleartext. If a release ships with an ATS/cleartextTraffic exception to 'make it work', the same interception works on any coffee-shop network.
findings.impact: Session hijack (bearer JWT), credential theft, PII disclosure (elder safety data).
findings.recommendation: app.config.js resolving apiBaseUrl per EAS profile; HTTPS (Railway) for preview/prod; keep the LAN IP only for local dev and never add a global cleartext exception.
findings.verification: self-verified (code + eas.json read; no per-profile extra found)

findings.title: Extractable demo credentials documented as bypassing the login rate limiter
findings.description: Hardcoded demo logins (elder/12345678, helper/123456789) ship in the JS bundle; the code comment states they bypass the login rate limiter (web parity).
findings.exploit_scenario: Extract credentials from the published bundle, script unlimited /auth/login (limiter bypassed by design), then use the demo session to spam SOS/messages/reports or probe authenticated endpoints at scale.
findings.impact: Abuse platform + noisy-neighbour harm to real users; reputational risk from SOS spam.
findings.recommendation: Server-side: separate throttle + reduced privileges (no SOS, no reports) for demo accounts. Client: exclude the demo card from production builds (__DEV__ gate or EAS env flag).
findings.verification: self-verified (component read; backend controls out of this repo's scope)

excluded_by_policy: Deep-link screens without client-side auth guard — precedent #5: client-side JS does not need auth, the server is the boundary (kept as a /review UX finding, not a security finding)
